messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: cross-validation fit
parts:
On Tue, Dec 4, 2018 at 3:55 AM <rico...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi Phil,

I am using cross-validation in mirt:
(1) Trained model: the model trained on one part of the sample and then
(2) Tested model: the fixed parameter estimates from the trained model are tested on an independent part of the sample.

I would like to evaluate fit on the independent sample using
(1) M2: rmsea, tli, cfi,
(2) M2: srmsr and individual item residual correlations,
(3) personfit Zh,
(4) itemfit S_X2.

I computed the rmsea, tli, and cfi using the internal functions with the m2-statistic and the sample size (non-zero/non-perfect scores) from the test model and the degrees from the training model (correct?);

I don't really understand this part. What you should do is take the item parameter estimates from the training model and simply use these as the parameter estimates in the tested mode. Computing M2() on the new model should give some indication about the goodness of fit of the new data using old parameters, while the same approaches should work for all the other statistics as well. 

 
however, how shall I proceed to compute points (2), (3), (4) correctly?

In the same way as you would any other cross-validated model. Not quite sure what the issue is here, though perhaps you're thinking of something that I am not. 
 

Perhaps, a cross-validation function (or boosting) could be implemented in mirt in the future (I would certainly use it!)

Sure, but as you note what to look for in terms of validation is variable. 

Phil
 

Best,
Rico

Oh, sorry, I assumed that it all made sense. messages.subject: Re: cross-validation fit
parts:
You're right, you should be using the df from the previous models. But in mirt, unlike some other software, it's easy to setup models to stop right at the starting values. Just pass TOL = NaN to mirt() and everything will terminate as is, where the new model will still have the same freely estimated parameters as your training model. HTH. 

Phil

messages.subject: Re: cross-validation fit
parts:
Hi again,

I used the TOL=NaN method and now the df are correct; but I am unsure about the M2-statistic. Why does it differ between using the TOL=NaN method and the pars$est=F method? In this case, the m2 statistic should be correct for fit2 since I am using the same data; however, with my real models I run into the situation when my fixed-estimate validation models have better fit than if the are freely estimated? Example below which used the same data for all three:

#Train
fit <- mirt(data,1)
pars <- mod2values(fit)

fit2 <- mirt(data,1,pars=pars,TOL=NaN)

pars$est <- F
fit3 <- mirt(data,1,pars=pars)

> M2(fit)
          M2  df p RMSEA RMSEA_5 RMSEA_95  SRMSR    TLI    CFI
stats 101205 486 0 0.144  0.1432   0.1447 0.1084 0.6636 0.6862
> M2(fit2)
          M2  df p RMSEA RMSEA_5 RMSEA_95  SRMSR    TLI    CFI
stats 101205 486 0 0.144  0.1432   0.1447 0.1084 0.6636 0.6862
> M2(fit3)
          M2  df p  RMSEA RMSEA_5 RMSEA_95  SRMSR   TLI    CFI
stats 122886 630 0 0.1393  0.1386     0.14 0.1084 0.685 0.6191


Rico

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: cross-validation fit
parts:
Because M2 computes the collapsed moments based on the orthogonal compliment of the freely estimated parameters. Hence, you can't use the pars$est <- FALSE approach, because it's computing the M2 statistic based on parameters you are assuming to be fixed and known a priori. Other stats may not be this limited, but for the M2 you'd have to leave these parameters as estimated (i.e., your fit2).

Phil

On Tue, Dec 4, 2018 at 3:55 AM <rico...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi Phil,

I am using cross-validation in mirt:
(1) Trained model: the model trained on one part of the sample and then
(2) Tested model: the fixed parameter estimates from the trained model are tested on an independent part of the sample.

I would like to evaluate fit on the independent sample using
(1) M2: rmsea, tli, cfi,
(2) M2: srmsr and individual item residual correlations,
(3) personfit Zh,
(4) itemfit S_X2.

I computed the rmsea, tli, and cfi using the internal functions with the m2-statistic and the sample size (non-zero/non-perfect scores) from the test model and the degrees from the training model (correct?);

I don't really understand this part. What you should do is take the item parameter estimates from the training model and simply use these as the parameter estimates in the tested mode. Computing M2() on the new model should give some indication about the goodness of fit of the new data using old parameters, while the same approaches should work for all the other statistics as well. 

 
however, how shall I proceed to compute points (2), (3), (4) correctly?

In the same way as you would any other cross-validated model. Not quite sure what the issue is here, though perhaps you're thinking of something that I am not. 
 

Perhaps, a cross-validation function (or boosting) could be implemented in mirt in the future (I would certainly use it!)

Sure, but as you note what to look for in terms of validation is variable. 

Phil
 

Best,
Rico

Den fredag 7 december 2018 kl. 18:20:02 UTC+1 skrev Phil Chalmers:
If you are passing TOL=NaN there's no need to change the estimator. Just use the defaults. I'll throw an error about this in the future. 

Phil


On Fri, Dec 7, 2018 at 11:36 AM <rico...@gmail.com> wrote:
Also, I am getting this error when I try to use TOL=NaN for a MHRM estimator:

Error in if (all(abs(gamma * correction) < TOL)) conv <- conv + 1L else conv <- 0L : 
  missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed



Den fredag 7 december 2018 kl. 15:50:48 UTC+1 skrev rico...@gmail.com:
Hi again,

I used the TOL=NaN method and now the df are correct; but I am unsure about the M2-statistic. Why does it differ between using the TOL=NaN method and the pars$est=F method? In this case, the m2 statistic should be correct for fit2 since I am using the same data; however, with my real models I run into the situation when my fixed-estimate validation models have better fit than if the are freely estimated? Example below which used the same data for all three:

#Train
fit <- mirt(data,1)
pars <- mod2values(fit)

fit2 <- mirt(data,1,pars=pars,TOL=NaN)

pars$est <- F
fit3 <- mirt(data,1,pars=pars)

> M2(fit)
          M2  df p RMSEA RMSEA_5 RMSEA_95  SRMSR    TLI    CFI
stats 101205 486 0 0.144  0.1432   0.1447 0.1084 0.6636 0.6862
> M2(fit2)
          M2  df p RMSEA RMSEA_5 RMSEA_95  SRMSR    TLI    CFI
stats 101205 486 0 0.144  0.1432   0.1447 0.1084 0.6636 0.6862
> M2(fit3)
          M2  df p  RMSEA RMSEA_5 RMSEA_95  SRMSR   TLI    CFI
stats 122886 630 0 0.1393  0.1386     0.14 0.1084 0.685 0.6191


Rico

Den onsdag 5 december 2018 kl. 19:04:43 UTC+1 skrev rico...@gmail.com:

Den onsdag 5 december 2018 kl. 16:13:45 UTC+1 skrev Phil Chalmers:
You're right, you should be using the df from the previous models. But in mirt, unlike some other software, it's easy to setup models to stop right at the starting values. Just pass TOL = NaN to mirt() and everything will terminate as is, where the new model will still have the same freely estimated parameters as your training model. HTH. 

Phil


On Wed, Dec 5, 2018 at 3:19 AM <rico...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi Phil,

Oh, sorry, I assumed that it all made sense. The attached image shows the M2* estimates for the same model on 5 independent samples: first freely estimated and second based on the fixed estimates from the training models (i.e., k-fold cval). As you can see the fit is often better for the fixed estimates than for the free (due to no df being used in the estimation). Intuitively, this feels wrong. If I use the df from the freely estimated models the estimates seem more representative of reality. What is your opinion?

Rico
